france24fr.title: Incendies : "Ceux qui nient le réchauffement doivent ouvrir les yeux", selon le commandant Lecras
france24fr.description: Le méga-feu de Gironde, stabilisé mais non maîtrisé, mobilise encore les sapeurs-pompiers, mercredi. Parmi eux, le commandant Yaël Lecras, qui alerte sur une profession éprouvée par le dérèglement climatique et le manque de moyens.

france24fr.title: Comores : six médinas inscrites au patrimoine mondial de l’Unesco
france24fr.description: Quatre nouveaux sites africains ont rejoint le patrimoine mondial de l'UNESCO. Aux Comores, six médinas historiques font leur entrée sur la prestigieuse liste. Une première pour l'archipel, dont certaines remontent au XIIᵉ siècle.

france24fr.title: Côte d'Ivoire : la coupe de cheveux imposée à l'école fait débat
france24fr.description: En Côte d’Ivoire, dans de nombreux établissements scolaires, les élèves, filles comme garçons, sont tenus de porter les cheveux courts.  Une règle en vigueur depuis des années, mais aujourd’hui contestée, notamment par de jeunes filles. Une pétition, lancée anonymement, début juillet et largement relayée sur les réseaux sociaux, demande aux autorités d’autoriser les élèves à conserver leurs cheveux naturels

france24fr.title: Incendies en Gironde : à bord du Caracal, l’hélicoptère qui surveille le feu en temps réel
france24fr.description: La lutte acharnée contre les flammes dans le Sud-Ouest nécessite une adaptation constante et des moyens hors normes, notamment la nuit, quand les bombardiers d'eau ne peuvent pas travailler. Les équipes de France 2 ont pu embarquer à bord du Caracal, chargé de surveiller en temps réel l'intensité du feu.

france24fr.title: Incendie en Gironde : comment les pompiers gèrent-ils les reprises de feu ?
france24fr.description: Une importante reprise de feu a mobilisé mercredi les pompiers à Lanton, en Gironde, aidés de nombreux volontaires, a constaté une équipe de l'AFP, alors que cette journée caniculaire complique la lutte contre le mégafeu qui a ravagé 42.000 hectares dans le département.

france24fr.title: Guerre des espions sur Telegram : pourquoi le FSB s’en prend à Pavel Durov
france24fr.description: Le FSB a lancé un mandat d’arrêt, mercredi, contre Pavel Durov, le fondateur de Telegram. Le service russe de renseignement lui reproche d’avoir laissé le champ libre à des espions ukrainiens qui recruteraient des adolescents russes pour des actes de sabotage. Ils passeraient notamment par une célèbre chaîne de rencontre sur Telegram.

france24fr.title: Levée de boucliers contre la Fifa, sommée de renoncer aux investissements privés
france24fr.description: Au lendemain de l'annonce de son projet d'ouverture aux investisseurs privés via la création d'une société dédiée, la Fifa est sous le feu des critiques politiques et sportives mercredi, avec en première ligne l'UEFA et l'Union européenne.

france24fr.title: L'avant-après saisissant des incendies dévastateurs en Gironde et dans les Landes
france24fr.description: Le mégafeu qui a brûlé 42.000 hectares en Gironde depuis le 22 juillet est "toujours stabilisé" mercredi matin après une seconde nuit "calme", a-t-on appris auprès de la préfecture du département.

france24fr.title: Guerre au Moyen-Orient : les frappes américano-saoudiennes en Irak font au moins 20 morts
france24fr.description: Les ⁠Etats-Unis et l'Arabie saoudite ont mené dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi des ⁠frappes en Irak contre des ​groupes armés pro-iraniens auxquels ils imputent des attaques de drones contre des infrastructures pétrolières du royaume wahhabite.

france24fr.title: Incendie en Espagne : situation "favorable", les 12 prochaines heures "décisives"
france24fr.description: Avec une situation "favorable" de la lutte contre l'incendie de forêts près de Madrid, plus de 20.000 personnes évacuées ont retrouvé leur domicile, les 12 prochaines heures étant "décisives" pour maîtriser le feu qui sévit depuis près d'une semaine, a annoncé mercredi le Premier ministre espagnol Pedro Sánchez.

france24fr.title: Guinée : décès d'un adolescent emprisonné pour fraude au Baccalauréat
france24fr.description: En Guinée, un adolescent emprisonné pour fraude au baccalauréat est décédé quelques jours après son incarcération. Détenu à la maison d'arrêt de Kindia, il avait été condamné à un mois de prison ferme avec plusieurs autres candidats.

france24fr.title: Projet de la Fifa : une réunion d'urgence convoquée par les instances européennes
france24fr.description: Sous l'égide de l'UEFA, les fédérations européennes du football vont se réunir, mercredi, pour débattre du projet de la Fifa d'ouvrir la porte aux investisseurs privés via la création d'une société. "Un projet qui pourrait profondément transformer l'équilibre de notre sport", selon la ministre française,des Sports, Marina Ferrari.

france24fr.title: Au Cameroun, la longue absence de Paul Biya fait polémique
france24fr.description: Au Cameroun, Paul Biya n'a plus été vu en public depuis le 7 juin, soit 50 jours d'absence. À 93 ans, le président camerounais alimente les spéculations sur sa gouvernance. L'opposition dénonce un pays en "pilotage automatique".

zeit.description: Elena und Felix sind verliebt, trennen sich, versuchen es wieder. Die Zweifel bleiben – bis zu diesem einen Augenblick. Ein Paar erzählt vom Make-it-or-break-it-Moment.

zeit.description: In Niedersachsen können Laien in Wahlausschüssen über Kandidaturen entscheiden. AfD-Verbot durch die Hintertür oder demokratisch angemessen? Die Aufregung ist groß.

zeit.description: Die K-Pop-Band BTS kritisiert eine neue Grammy-Preiskategorie für asiatischen Pop. Musik dürfe nicht anhand von Sprachen von Regionen definiert werden, sagen die Musiker.

zeit.title: Wirtschaftskrise in Kuba: Kuba öffnet mehrere Wirtschaftssektoren für Privatfirmen
zeit.description: Angesichts der Wirtschaftskrise hat die kommunistische Führung Kubas einige Sektoren für private Unternehmen geöffnet. Dazu zählen Apotheken, Tankstellen und Altenpflege.

zeit.title: Bundestag: Unionsfraktion wählt Thorsten Frei zum Vorsitzenden
zeit.description: Die Abgeordneten von CDU und CSU haben Thorsten Frei mit 91,9 Prozent zu ihrem neuen Vorsitzenden gewählt. Weitere Personalveränderungen plant der Bundeskanzler nicht.

nzz.title: Swiss musste aufgrund eines beschädigten Kopfhörer-Ladecase notlanden
nzz.description: Auf dem Flug von Zürich nach New York hat sich Rauch in der Businessclass entwickelt. Grund war eine kleine Powerbank, die in einen Sitz gerutscht war und sich erhitzt hatte.

nzz.title: Ein Gruss aus der Vergangenheit: Absenderin einer Flaschenpost nach siebzig Jahren gefunden
nzz.description: Fast siebzig Jahre lang lag eine Flaschenpost unter dem Rheinufer in Oberwesel. Nachdem Bauarbeiter sie zufällig freigebaggert hatten, begann eine Spurensuche.

nzz.title: Der Riss in Polens rechter Opposition vertieft sich: Der Abweichler Morawiecki gründet eine eigene Parlamentsfraktion
nzz.description: Im Streit verschiedener Flügel der grössten polnischen Oppositionspartei Recht und Gerechtigkeit ist der Bruch komplett. Die beiden Seiten gehen hart aufeinander los.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: USA verhängen neue Sanktionen gegen Iran +++ Trump kündigt nach iranischer Attacke Vergeltung an
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Der Ausschluss kommunaler AfD-Kandidaten ist ein Warnsignal: Die wehrhafte Demokratie ist an der falschen Stelle wehrhaft
nzz.description: In Niedersachsen können vier AfD-Politiker nicht zur Wahl antreten, weil Wahlausschüsse Zweifel an ihrer Verfassungstreue hatten. Die Politisierung solcher Gremien ist bedenklich. Ihnen sollte kein Urteil über die inhaltlichen Positionen eines Kandidaten zustehen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Zwei Feuerwehrleute kommen bei Waldbrand in Kreta ums Leben +++ Hitze erschwert Löscharbeiten in Frankreich
nzz.description: Wo ist es zurzeit besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Die neuesten Meldungen über Hitzerekorde, Dürren und Brände in Europa.

nzz.title: 53-Jähriger erhält 13 Jahre und 5 Monate Freiheitsstrafe für tödlichen Messerangriff in der Lugano-Bar
nzz.description: Das Bezirksgericht Zürich hat einen Mann, der im August 2023 einen Barkeeper an der Langstrasse erstach, wegen  Mordes verurteilt.

nzz.title: Eine Sek-Schülerin kommt regelmässig zu spät, schläft im Unterricht ein oder vernachlässigt die Hausaufgaben. Was dann passiert, löst einen Rechtsstreit aus
nzz.description: Die Schule greift zu disziplinarischen Massnahmen. Doch die Eltern wehren sich vor Gericht.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Historische Brände in Europa: Es braucht ein Umdenken
nzz.description: Extreme Hitze und Trockenheit sind die neue Realität in Zeiten des Klimawandels. Waldbrände wüten in Europa. Aber wir sind nicht machtlos. Kluge Landschaftsplanung hilft jetzt mehr als abstrakte Klimapolitik.

nzz.title: Er vergewaltigte und ermordete eine Prostituierte, nun erhält er eine Genugtuung von 175 000 Franken – wie ist das möglich?
nzz.description: Rund sieben Jahre sass ein jugendlicher Mörder unrechtmässig in Haft. Der Fall hatte politische Folgen bis ins Bundeshaus. Der Kanton Aargau hat sich nun mit ihm geeinigt.

nzz.title: Die deutsche Autokrise verschärft sich. Nun baut auch BMW Tausende Stellen ab
nzz.description: Der Münchner Konzern reagiert mit einem Sparprogramm auf die anhaltende Schwäche der Branche. Der Stellenabbau betrifft vorwiegend Arbeitsplätze in Deutschland.

nzz.title: Die Zeichen standen auf Aufbruch in Italiens Fussball. Doch dann ging erst einmal alles schief
nzz.description: Absagen, Zusagen – und eine bemerkenswerte Rückkehr: Die Suche nach einem neuen Trainer für die Squadra Azzurra verläuft chaotisch und endet sehr italienisch. Protokoll eines aufreibenden Monats.

nzz.title: Vorsichtige Freude über Gorillanachwuchs im Zoo Zürich
nzz.description: Die Geburt gilt als gutes Zeichen für das Funktionieren der neu zusammengesetzten Gruppe. Doch Todesfälle im Zoo Basel zeigen, wie fragil die Situation ist.

nzz.title: Die UBS startet ein neues Programm für Aktienrückkäufe – just bevor die politische Debatte um das Eigenkapital wieder losgeht
nzz.description: Im zweiten Quartal hat die Grossbank ein Konzernergebnis von 2,8 Milliarden Dollar erzielt. Die Aktien legen an der Börse zu.

nzz.title: Eklat im Tessin: Regierungspräsident Claudio Zali gibt sein Amt ab und sieht sich als Opfer medialer Lynchjustiz
nzz.description: Der Druck auf den Lega-Politiker Claudio Zali wurde zu gross. Wegen diverser Skandale scheidet er per Ende September aus der Tessiner Kantonsregierung aus.

nzz.title: Überraschung aus Teheran: Mit einem Raketenangriff beenden die Iraner die Feuerpause
nzz.description: In der Nacht auf Mittwoch hat Iran eine amerikanische Militärbasis in Jordanien angegriffen. Die Islamische Republik will den Druck auf Washington erhöhen. Doch der neue Offensivkurs birgt grosse Risiken.

spiegel.title: Irankrieg: »Dass Benjamin Netanyahu wieder in Washington ist, erhöht das Risiko«
spiegel.description: Droht im Irankrieg die nächste Eskalation? Der Politikwissenschaftler Hamidreza Azizi erklärt, welche Optionen beide Seiten nun haben, wie es in der Straße von Hormus weitergehen könnte und wie es den Menschen in Iran geht.

spiegel.title: Merz' Kandidat holt ein gutes Ergebnis. Dann entlädt sich der Frust der Abgeordneten
spiegel.description: Bei der Wahl von Thorsten Frei zum neuen Unionsfraktionschef zeigen die Abgeordneten Disziplin. Doch Kanzler Friedrich Merz muss sich massiver Kritik stellen, die Rede ist von einem »Scherbengericht«.

spiegel.title: Florenz: Haben eigentlich die Italiener die Cola erfunden?
spiegel.description: Ist Cola gar nicht amerikanisch? In einem toskanischen Kloster ist ein Zettel für eine Mixtur aufgetaucht, die moderner Cola auffällig ähnelt – inklusive Colanüssen und Kokablättern. Es gibt aber einen großen Unterschied.

spiegel.title: Lea Wagner: ARD-Reporterin ist Mutter geworden
spiegel.description: Ein Millionenpublikum sah bei der Fußball-WM der schwangeren Lea Wagner beim Moderieren zu. Nun ist ihre Tochter geboren.

spiegel.title: Waldbrände in Europa: Warum es so wenige Löschflugzeuge gibt
spiegel.description: In Südeuropa wüten heftige Feuer. Löscharbeiten aus der Luft hätten Schlimmeres verhindern können, sagen Piloten. Doch viele Flugzeuge sind veraltet, ein neues Löschkit von Airbus ist kaum erprobt.

spiegel.title: »Bitteres Fest« von Pedro Almodóvar: Geklautes Leid, einträgliches Leid?
spiegel.description: Könnte es sein, dass viele Autorenfilmer die Lebensgeschichten von Freunden und Bekannten ausbeuten? Darüber denkt der Autorenfilmer Pedro Almodóvar in seinem neuen Werk nach.

spiegel.title: Wahlpflicht in Australien: Darf eine Regierung ihre Bürger zwingen, wählen zu gehen?
spiegel.description: IIn Australien gilt seit 1924 die Wahlpflicht. Seither wurde die 90-Prozent-Marke bei der Wahlbeteiligung nur einmal unterschritten. Experten sprechen von einer Stabilisierung der politischen Mitte.

spiegel.title: Gianni Infantino will Teilverkauf der Fußball-WM und setzt Fifa-Mitglieder unter Druck
spiegel.description: Fifa-Boss Gianni Infantino will Anteile an der Fußball-WM verkaufen – nach SPIEGEL-Informationen geht sein Plan deutlich weiter als vom Weltverband kommuniziert: Er hat den Nationalverbänden eine Frist gesetzt.

spiegel.title: Waldbrände in Südeuropa: Zwei Feuerwehrleute sterben auf Kreta
spiegel.description: Waldbrände haben Südeuropa weiter fest im Griff. In der Türkei haben einige Evakuierte ihre Häuser verloren, auf Kreta umzingelten die Flammen ein Feuerwehrfahrzeug. Zwei Einsatzkräfte starben.

spiegel.title: Miley Cyrus: Sängerin und Schauspielerin spricht über Zweifel zum Beginn ihrer Karriere
spiegel.description: Als »Hannah Montana« wurde sie zu einem der kommerziell erfolgreichsten Popstars ihrer Zeit. Doch Miley Cyrus sagt, sie habe sich für eine Weile selbst verloren.

spiegel.title: Dieter Reiter: Disziplinarverfahren gegen Münchens Ex-OB beendet
spiegel.description: Erst kostete die Affäre um bezahlte, nicht genehmigte Aufgaben beim FC Bayern den Rathauschef den Job. Dann drohte Dieter Reiter Ärger mit der oberbayerischen Regierung. Dieses Verfahren wurde nun aber ad acta gelegt.

spiegel.title: Hamburg: Transport der neuen Sternbrücke hat begonnen
spiegel.description: In Hamburg kommt ein Großprojekt in die entscheidende Phase: Die tonnenschwere Sternbrücke hat ihr erstes Ziel erreicht. Am Donnerstag wartet die nächste Herausforderung.

spiegel.title: Berlin - Wahlkampf nach CSD-Anschlag: Unterwegs mit CDU-Spitzenkandidat Stefan Evers
spiegel.description: Der Anschlag auf den CSD überschattet den Berliner Wahlkampf. CDU-Spitzenkandidat Stefan Evers ist selbst schwul und will mit dem Thema Sicherheit punkten – auch bei der queeren Community.

spiegel.title: Heftige Feuer in Europa: Werden irgendwann die Flammen vor Potsdam stehen? Ein Experte klärt auf
spiegel.description: Europaweit wächst die Brandgefahr, warnt der Ökologe Thomas Hickler, nicht nur im Süden. Er sieht den deutschen Wald vor einer Zeitenwende.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Fraktionssitzung der Union, Gianni Infantinos Gier, der Stellenabbau bei BMW
spiegel.description: Die Unionsfraktion hat einen neuen Chef, aber Ärger mit Kanzler Merz. Der Fifa-Präsident will Investoren an der Fußball-WM beteiligen. Und bei BMW und Porsche fallen Tausende Stellen weg. Das ist die Lage am Mittwochabend.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz will sich bei Jens Spahn bedanken – und ihn nicht fallen lassen
spiegel.description: In der Personalrochade ist ein weiterer Posten fest: Thorsten Frei folgt als Unionsfraktionschef auf den zurückgetretenen Jens Spahn. Für Kanzler Merz und CSU-Chef Söder ist Spahn damit aber offenbar nicht abgemeldet.

spiegel.title: Kinder ohne Smartphone lesen besser
spiegel.description: Viel Meinung, wenig Experimente: So fassen Psychologinnen aus Los Angeles den Forschungsstand zur Auswirkung digitaler Geräte auf die Schulbildung zusammen. Ihre Versuche sollen Licht in die Sache bringen.

spiegel.description: Videos zeigen, wie Bill Oliver im kanadischen Parlament einen geplanten Gesetzentwurf kritisiert. Dann folgt ein Satz in typischem Stil künstlicher Intelligenz. Wochen später kassiert der Politiker dafür Spott im Netz.

Claudio Zali, membre de la Lega, était visé par une enquête pénale et éclaboussé par des révélations embarrassantes. Le président du gouvernement tessinois annonce quitter son poste fin septembre. C’est un UDC qui le remplacera

Pour permettre aux seniors de vivre plus longtemps chez eux, le canton de Vaud offre une aide financière de 3000 francs pour des petits travaux d’aménagement. observador.title: BTS não vão concorrer à 69ª edição dos Grammy
observador.description: Decisão anunciada por todos os membros dos BTS. Fãs do grupo de K-pop consideram nova categoria forma de segregação capaz de afastar artistas asiáticos das categorias mais prestigiadas dos prémios.

observador.title: Cantor Carlão veste tshirt com símbolo terrorista?
observador.description: Circula nas redes sociais uma alegação falsa sobre o músico Carlão. Nem a UE nem a ONU classificam a Antifa como organização terrorista.

observador.title: Açores investem 22 milhões em saúde convencionada
observador.description: 2,5 milhões de exames e tratamentos realizados em 2025. Análises clínicas e medicina física lideram, mas Imagiologia falha por falta de especialistas.

observador.title: ULS Algarve: 1,2 milhões de euros por cobrar a estrangeiros
observador.description: Britânicos, franceses e alemães são os principais utilizadores das urgências algarvias. Auditores recomendam cobrança antecipada e criação de "check-out" obrigatório na saída.

observador.title: Morreu Eduardo Trigo, figura da comunicação social, aos 92
observador.description: O antigo presidente da Notícias de Portugal, cuja fusão com a ANOP originou a Lusa em 1986, será cremado esta quinta-feira em Oeiras. Também foi membro da Alta Autoridade para a Comunicação Social.

observador.title: Lisboa aprova loteamento da Unidade de Execução da Matinha
observador.description: CML deu "luz verde" ao projeto, para criar um novo bairro multifuncional, de 2 mil milhões de euros, e promover "mais habitação" em Marvila. PS, Livre e BE votaram contra. PCP e Chega abstiveram-se.

observador.title: Câmara de Oeiras alerta para burla com casas municipais
observador.description: Burla consiste no pedido de pagamentos para reservar casas municipals que estariam, supostamente, à venda. A autarquia esclarece que as casas municipais apenas podem ser vendidas pela própria câmara.

observador.title: Homem morre em colisão de mota com automóvel
observador.description: Sinistro ocorreu na cidade sadina e o alerta foi dado às 15h26. Óbito do motociclista foi declarado no local, por um médico do Hospital do Litoral Alentejano. Socorro envolveu 21 operacionais.

observador.title: Jovem em prisão preventiva por atear fogo em Ponte de Lima
observador.description: O jovem confessou ter ateado os cinco focos de incêndio em Ponte de Lima. Depois de ter sido presente a tribunal, ficou em prisão preventiva. A polícia apreendeu dois isqueiros e um telemóvel.

observador.title: 16 anos e meio por matar idoso à paulada em Águeda
observador.description: O arguido, de 45 anos, foi condenado pelo Tribunal de Aveiro por homicídio qualificado. ADN e impressões digitais numa garrafa de cerveja ligaram-no ao crime, cometido em julho de 2025.

observador.title: Produção de lixo aumentou em cidades servidas pela Lipor
observador.description: Munícipes produziram mais 1,9% de lixo. Capitação foi de 117,8 kg por habitante ao ano e apenas 4.357 toneladas foram recolhidas em aterro. Empresa pede mais participação no processo de reciclagem.

observador.title: Metas privadas do PRR praticamente cumpridas
observador.description: A um mês do prazo terminar, governo prevê execução total do PRR, mas alerta para esforço na reta final. Já Pedro Dominguinhos revela que o maior desafio centra-se na conclusão de obras públicas.

observador.title: Air France-KLM traz apoio da Delta para oferta pela TAP
observador.description: Americana Delta Airlines "apoia e está alinhada" com a proposta da Air France-KLM para a TAP a pensar no mercado do Atlantico Norte. Lufthansa reafirma que Lisboa será hub para a América Latina.

observador.title: Japão. Os testemunhos dos sobreviventes do sismo de 6,8
observador.description: Enquanto as equipas de socorro continuam a procurar sobreviventes, os habitantes das zonas afetadas pelo sismo relatam momentos de pânico, fugas de carro e tentativas de resgate durante as réplicas.

observador.title: Uma "péssima notícia" nas bombas e os impérios da beleza
observador.description: Mais uma semana de aumentos dos combustíveis. O Governo reconhece a "péssima notícia" e está "atento", mas a oposição pede mais. Perfumes & Companhia e Primor unem-se, mas há mais negócios no setor.

observador.title: Ariana Grande processa hackers por alegado roubo de músicas
observador.description: A cantora recorreu a um tribunal de Los Angeles para identificar os responsáveis por fugas de músicas, fotos e vídeos desde 2011, incluindo 45 músicas roubadas só em 2023.

observador.title: Tribunal trava restrições a autocarros em Sintra
observador.description: Operadores turísticos contestam medidas em vigor desde 8 de julho que proíbem autocarros de parar na Volta do Duche. Câmara foi notificada esta quarta-feira.

observador.title: Torres Vedras inicia requalificação de aqueduto medieval
observador.description: Monumento nacional desde 1910, a estrutura do século XIV apresenta troços em risco de colapso. Obras têm 15 meses de prazo para travar a degradação.

elpais.description: El presidente ceutí advierte de que la situación es de “colapso” en la ciudad autónoma y pide al Gobierno una respuesta “contundente y sin dilación”

nyt.description: The future of artificial intelligence depends on finding more skilled humans for some very physical jobs.

nyt.description: In the latest example, the Energy Department will convert a shuttered Cold War-era uranium enrichment facility into a data center campus and gas plants.

nyt.description: The request suggests the intense personal involvement of President Trump in investigating one of his longtime critics, the former F.B.I. director James B. Comey.

nyt.description: A seven-figure settlement is announced two days before a scheduled Senate committee vote on Todd Blanche’s nomination to be attorney general.

nyt.description: The State Department under Secretary of State Marco Rubio has deported Cubans to Africa. Now it’s negotiating with a South American country.

nyt.title: Matt Damon’s Biceps in That ‘Odyssey’ Fight Scene? They’re Hers.
nyt.description: Devyn Dalton, a 4-foot-6 woman, is the leading man’s stunt double in Christopher Nolan’s summer blockbuster.

nyt.description: The veteran performer is making waves as a blind servant in “The Odyssey.” But he was worried that a scene with dogs would make him the most hated actor in movies.

nyt.title: Why Republicans Aren’t Funding the Texas Senate Race Yet
nyt.description: The peculiar dynamic is playing out in Texas, where the fate of the Republican nominee, Ken Paxton, will help decide which party controls the U.S. Senate.

nyt.title: Obama Endorses Josh Turek in Iowa Senate Race With Basketball Video
nyt.description: The former president is trying to help Josh Turek net a Senate seat in Iowa, which Democrats see as one of their best pickup opportunities of the midterms.

nyt.title: Summer of Heat, Fires and Storms Is a Reckoning for Europe on Climate
nyt.description: The continent is experiencing some of its biggest fires and highest temperatures ever. Residents are fleeing, leaders are struggling to respond and “it will get worse,” one climate expert said.

nyt.title: European Wildfires Amplified by Emptying Countryside and Fewer Farms
nyt.description: A warming planet and a shift away from farming have set the stage for larger fires on the continent. “We must learn to coexist with them,” one report said.

nyt.title: Wildfires Slow in France and Spain, but Worse May Be Ahead
nyt.description: Firefighters have contained vast wildfires in both countries, but winds are high and temperatures rising. Spain’s prime minister said the next 12 hours would be “decisive.”

nyt.title: Sanctions Bill Would Give Trump Sweeping New Tariff Powers
nyt.description: A bipartisan bill in the Senate would allow President Trump to impose tariffs on the biggest importers of Russian energy.

nyt.title: Trump’s Tariffs Are Sending Some Companies Back to China
nyt.description: For some U.S. brands seeking a location for their factories, the economic logic is once again pointing to China.

nyt.title: Canada’s Answer to Trump’s Tariffs: More Energy Deals With Europe
nyt.description: The Carney government’s agreement with a German natural gas company will also reduce Europe’s dependence on a Qatari supply made more uncertain by war.

nyt.title: Can This Man Stop the Mamdani Agenda?

npr.title: 'Taiwan Travelogue' rethinks history, colonialism, and identity
npr.description: The author and translator of Taiwan Travelogue, the winner of the 2026 International Booker Prize, discuss identity and history amid the debate over Taiwan's colonial ties to Japan and escalating geopolitical pressure from China.

npr.title: Greetings from an isolated region in northern Pakistan's Hindu Kush mountains
npr.description: Chitral borders Afghanistan and isn't easy to reach. Breathtaking views abound in this remote mountainous region — as do rockslides and avalanches.

npr.title: U.S. and Iran resume attacks. And, Fauci to face Senate questions on COVID pandemic

npr.title: Iran resumes missile attacks as U.S. and Saudis strike Tehran-backed militias in Iraq
npr.description: The flare-up on multiple fronts raised the risk of a return to all-out war, underscoring the difficulty of winding down a five-month conflict that has jolted the world economy.

npr.title: In France and Spain, the battle to contain wildfires faces another heatwave
npr.description: Authorities in France and Spain say some of their wildfires are mostly contained, but others are blazing on and a new wave of extreme heat is raising fears of more fires to come.

npr.title: Death toll rises to 18 as rescuers comb through quake rubble in southwestern Japan
npr.description: Soldiers and emergency workers combed through a badly damaged shopping mall and collapsed houses looking for trapped survivors Wednesday after a powerful earthquake that killed at least 18 people, including a foreigner, in southwestern Japan.

npr.title: As Spain battles wildfires, its politicians battle over climate change's role
npr.description: Crews are still battling wildfires that broke out last week and have burned nearly 200,000 acres across Spain. The country is bracing for another round of extreme heat, with temperatures expected to top 100 degrees Fahrenheit starting Wednesday.

npr.title: Keiko Fujimori is inaugurated as Peru's president following a narrow election victory
npr.description: The 51-year-old daughter of the late former President Alberto Fujimori, Peru's new conservative leader has pledged to fight crime with an "iron fist."

npr.title: Trump meets Ukrainian, Israeli leaders as they pay respects to Lindsey Graham

npr.title: Ukraine negotiator: 'We have the upper hand'
npr.description: In an interview with NPR, one of Ukraine's top negotiators Sergiy Kyslytsya explains why Kyiv believes it now has the leverage to force Russia into serious negotiations.

phys-org.title: Curiosity Mars rover discovers field of honeycomb textures
phys-org.description: As NASA's Curiosity rover recently began climbing a Martian valley nicknamed "Valle Grande," it sent back images that were a familiar sight to mission scientists: honeycomb-like textures called polygonal fractures, each about 1.5–3 inches (4–8 centimeters) across. The mission has spotted small patches of these geometric shapes several times before, but nothing at the scale discovered in Valle Grande.

phys-org.title: Nepal's tiger numbers climb 20 percent to estimated 429: Survey
phys-org.description: Nepal's tiger population has risen by roughly 20% in the past four years to an estimated 429, officials said Wednesday, a conservation milestone despite challenges from human-wildlife conflict.

phys-org.title: Beyond wrinkles: New rule explains why growing shapes suddenly crumple
phys-org.description: Scientists have discovered a previously unknown law of geometry that explains why some growing surfaces, whether in nature or in engineered materials, suddenly stop being able to stay smooth and instead form dimples and folds. Until now, researchers believed they understood the geometric rules behind these shape changes, but this study reveals a new kind of "geometric frustration" that arises even when all the known rules are satisfied.

phys-org.title: An entire world of fungi nearly a third of a mile underground could affect carbon storage estimates
phys-org.description: Hundreds of feet below Earth's surface, rocks and water teem with fungi and support complex ecosystems of tiny organisms, according to a University of Michigan study that finds fungi are far more abundant deep underground than researchers previously thought.

phys-org.title: Shoppers would fork out more for better farm animal welfare
phys-org.description: Shoppers would pay more for their weekly groceries if it meant improved welfare for farm animals, according to new research from the University of Reading.

phys-org.title: Managing ecosystems under climate change using nature's hidden design
phys-org.description: Researchers at the Centre for Ecosystem Management (CEM), together with scientists from the Department of Fisheries and Oceans, Cornell University, Great Lakes Fishery Commission and the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources, have published a paper showing that ecosystems become more resilient to environmental change through "portfolio effects" operating across multiple levels of ecological organization.

phys-org.title: Biofilm clue opens route to anti-infection treatments of the future
phys-org.description: A multidisciplinary study has uncovered a critical component in the formation of biofilms, the complex structures used by bacteria to colonize surfaces. The research may have implications for future infection treatments, including for people with cystic fibrosis.

phys-org.title: More than half of England 'officially in drought': UK govt
phys-org.description: Just over half of England has been declared to be in drought after "record-low rainfall and exceptionally high temperatures," the U.K. government said Wednesday.

phys-org.title: In seconds, fiber optic cables detect earthquake size
phys-org.description: Scientists have discovered a new way to determine how big an earthquake may become just seconds after it begins. In a new study published in Nature Communications, researchers from the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) and Cal Poly Humboldt used signals picked up by fiber-optic cables—the same ones that deliver high-speed internet—to accurately estimate when a moderate to large earthquake is underway using data from the first four seconds of seismic wave arrivals.

phys-org.title: Non-monogamy may reduce jealousy overall, but feeling less desirable can still strain relationships
phys-org.description: Comparing yourself with your partner is more common than you'd think. Psychologists even have a term for it: mate value discrepancy (MVD), which is the gap between how attractive, smart or successful each partner feels compared with the other.

phys-org.title: Industrial noise may alter bluebird behavior but not cognitive ability
phys-org.description: Scientists have long wondered whether loud, human-caused noise interferes with wild animals' cognition—their ability to think and learn—by causing stress, distraction or making it harder for them to focus. The results of a novel study of eastern bluebirds conducted by a team of researchers at Penn State suggest that, at least in some cases, short-term noise doesn't affect them much.

phys-org.title: Shipwreck cargo reveals surprising global trade secrets of the 1600s
phys-org.description: Using cargo recovered from one of Australia's most infamous shipwrecks, new Curtin University-led research has revealed how surprisingly sophisticated global supply chains helped source and transport construction materials in the 17th century.

phys-org.title: Who says pollution clean-up has to pay for itself?
phys-org.description: In a world searching for more sustainable ways to manage waste, the promise of turning "trash into treasure" is hard to ignore. Take nitrate pollution, for example. Every year, nitrogen fertilizers help feed billions of people. But not all of that nitrogen stays where it is needed. Some is washed from farms into rivers, streams and groundwater, where it can contribute to environmental problems, including harmful algal blooms.

phys-org.title: Spain's three worst wildfires since 1961 happened in last two years
phys-org.description: The wildfire that engulfed Spain's Ávila region, northwest of the capital, Madrid, is now considered the largest in the country's modern history, with around 50,000 hectares (193 square miles) burned, the government said this week.

phys-org.title: Bringing complex field physics to the tabletop: A photonic stage for non-Abelian gauge fields
phys-org.description: For most theories in physics, the order of operations has little impact on the result. When setting a dial to a certain position, for example, it doesn't matter whether it's turned clockwise or counterclockwise—the result will always be the same. Yet for non-Abelian gauge theories, order does matter. These theories underpin the Standard Model, but to test their more subtle predictions, researchers have so far relied on enormous particle accelerators.

phys-org.title: Beyond bunny tourism: The hidden consequences of unregulated feeding of rabbits on Okunoshima island
phys-org.description: Feeding wild animals is a popular activity at tourist destinations. While these interactions often appear harmless, scientists are recognizing how supplemental feeding of wild animals can alter ecosystems in unexpected ways.

phys-org.title: Antarctic storms are becoming more frequent and intense, affecting sea ice
phys-org.description: Winters in Antarctica's Ross Sea have become stormier in recent decades, affecting sea-ice conditions and field operations, new University of Otago—Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka research shows.

phys-org.title: New antimicrobials could help tackle deadly drug-resistant infections
phys-org.description: Scientists at Imperial College London and the University of Manchester have developed a promising new way to create safer and more effective treatments for life-threatening fungal infections. The research, published today in Nature, describes a new family of antifungal agents that—when tested in mice—were more potent and less toxic than existing treatments.

undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing

Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers

One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

proj-syn.title: When Politicians Ignore Economic Expertise
proj-syn.description: As politicians encroach on areas that require technical knowledge, the risk of costly policy mistakes increases. The failures of Narendra Modi and Donald Trump show that when it comes to economic policymaking, political acumen is no substitute for a deep understanding of incentives, markets, and institutions.

proj-syn.title: The Beijing Model Meets the Brussels Effect
proj-syn.description: As Europe races to rebuild its industrial base, China is focusing more on influencing international standards and governance frameworks. The two powers are converging because neither can hope to claim a dominant position in the global energy transition by relying wholly on its traditional strengths.

proj-syn.title: The Mexican Government’s Economic Spin
proj-syn.description: By cherry-picking 12 data points that supposedly contradict top ratings agencies’ assessment of Mexico’s economy and fiscal outlook, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum recently presented a just-so story that should convince no one. A glimpse of what her list excludes makes that clear.

proj-syn.title: The Middle-Income Health Trap
proj-syn.description: Many countries that graduate from low- to middle-income status soon find themselves stuck in the position of being too rich to qualify for aid, too poor to secure reliable market-based financing, and too indebted to expand public-health spending. But it doesn't have to be this way.

proj-syn.title: Europe Is Fiddling While Rome Burns
proj-syn.description: Focusing only on emergency planning, disaster response, and recovery after each climate catastrophe is no longer enough in Europe. Policymakers urgently need to start mapping Europe’s long-term future, which will require a fundamental overhaul of its infrastructure, energy system, and major economic sectors.

proj-syn.title: Saving Democracy Requires Taxing Extreme Wealth
proj-syn.description: If lawmakers are serious about addressing the threat that dynastic wealth poses to American democracy, they can draw on considerable research that has gone into designing a wealth tax that avoids the pitfalls of other countries’ attempts. With the appearance of the world’s first trillionaire, there is no time to waste.

proj-syn.title: The AI Threat to Financial Stability
proj-syn.description: In episodes like the railroad boom and the dot-com bubble, creditors and shareholders were wiped out, because investment in a genuinely transformative technology outpaced any plausible near-term return. With the US financial system and asset markets having become a one-way bet on AI, such an outcome today could be catastrophic.

proj-syn.title: South Korea Bets on Industrial Policy Again
proj-syn.description: With industrial policy back in fashion worldwide, the question is not whether governments should intervene (they already do), but how they should proceed when they do not know in advance what will work. The answer lies in directed improvisation: creating the conditions for experimentation where it counts.

proj-syn.title: America Is Betting Against International Law
proj-syn.description: After cooperating with the International Criminal Court to indict Russian President Vladimir Putin for war crimes, the US has shifted to waging a scorched-earth campaign against the ICC in the name of protecting Israel. But rather than halting international law’s progress, the US is merely handing the pen to other countries.

proj-syn.title: The Therapist in Your Pocket
proj-syn.description: A new survey conducted by AXA and Ipsos shows that people are readily turning to AI chatbots to cope with mental-health problems. To ensure that these tools do more good than harm, health leaders, employers, insurers, and AI developers must take responsibility for steering them in a beneficial direction.

proj-syn.title: The Cost of Not Building Data Centers
proj-syn.description: In July, New York became the first state to enact a moratorium on new data centers, a path that other states may follow. But US policymakers, drawing lessons from past failures to make economy-wide investments in electrification and rare-earth processing, should weigh the strategic costs of not building essential infrastructure.

proj-syn.title: The Dangerous Spread of Jim Crow Nostalgia
proj-syn.description: With inaccurate claims about Black Americans’ poverty and crime rates having migrated from the far-right fringe to mainstream outlets like the Wall Street Journal, it is worth considering what the data actually say. Doing so will show that there is no empirical basis for such claims, only an ideological one.

proj-syn.title: The Gulf’s Push for AI-Led Governance
proj-syn.description: Governments around the world have spent decades outsourcing their ability to think to expensive consultants, gradually ceding the knowledge and judgment needed to govern effectively. AI may now offer a way to reverse that trend, and Gulf countries are providing an early glimpse of what that may look like.

proj-syn.title: India’s Exam Worriers Become Democracy Warriors
proj-syn.description: Generations of students in India have resigned themselves to the idea that the education system is primarily a sorting mechanism, which rewards compliance. But as recent protests showed, the system's rigidity, together with insufficient rewards in the form of good jobs, has rendered this approach untenable.

proj-syn.title: Why Business Leaders Are Souring on AI
proj-syn.description: Companies have poured billions of dollars into AI in anticipation of transformative productivity gains and cost savings, but the returns have yet to justify those investments. Rising costs, intellectual-property risks, and mounting cybersecurity threats call for a more disciplined approach to AI adoption.

proj-syn.title: How Burnham Can Make UK Devolution Work
proj-syn.description: Andy Burnham’s first 100 days as prime minister of the United Kingdom will need to be devoted to building the institutional architecture for his vision of devolved governance to succeed. The question is not where to concentrate decision-making authority, but how to ensure that different authorities are working together.

proj-syn.title: West Africa Needs Its Own Draghi Moment
proj-syn.description: Senegal’s debt crisis has exposed a deeper vulnerability within West Africa’s monetary union. Unable to devalue the shared currency, member countries must either endure painful internal adjustment or boost exports to earn the foreign currency they need to repay external creditors.

proj-syn.title: Will the Real Marco Rubio Please Stand Up?
proj-syn.description: Is US Secretary of State Marco Rubio an embattled champion of Venezuelan democracy within the Trump administration, or the public face of a strategy aimed at keeping the old regime in power? Six months after Nicolás Maduro’s ouster, his record suggests democratic restoration is no longer an American priority—if it ever was.
